utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I remind you, General, of the affirmation that you made which still applies. Ms. Residovic, do you have something more for us?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. No, Your Honours. What you had during the last week was enough, but I have a proposal to make. You received in evidence the plan for the deployment of the security forces that is Exhibit 1D177, the document has been shown to this witness and has been received with the draft translation. The court officer informed us that the official translation has arrived and I would like to ask the Chamber to replace the old draft with the official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. We foreshadowed that would occur and it will be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like that the witness is given these documents that he already had on Friday and we would like the assistance of the usher. While the witness is given these documents, Your Honours, I would like to remind you that on Friday at the beginning of the questioning of this witness, by mistake I didn't show you a document, for which the Defence proposes to only be marked for identification. I would like to ask now that you see the document in tab 144. And I would like to remind that this document - this is 92 bis statement of Kristo Zdravkovski which has been received in evidence as Exhibit 1D125, MFI and has been shown to the witness, Risto Galevski. In this statement, Kristo Zdravkovski, the head of the security sector in Bitola has mentioned that on the -- on the occasion of the Bitola events, criminal reports have been filed against around 100 persons. In line with that information, the Defence would like to ask you to look at the document in tab 145 which is 65 ter 1D583.1, page 1D5342, and the English is 1D5343. So the Defence asked from the Ministry of the Interior to inform us whether the report -- the criminal reports have been filed and what are persons against whom these criminal reports have been filed. I would like to ask you to look into the document in tab 146, which is 65 ter 583.2, 1D5344, and the English version is 1D5346. The ministry responded to us, quoting the exact number of criminal reports and the dates where these reports were filed to the basic prosecutor's office in Bitola with the names of the persons that have been reported. Given that we are following the decision that you made a couple of days ago and the directions that you gave in that sense, I would like to have this document, 65 ter 583.2, is marked -- to have this document marked for identification and the Defence will either call the witness or -- or present the original criminal reports. The Defence will additionally tender this in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not clear whether you want to tender something now or you're saying that you're going to tender the original criminal reports at some later time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since this 65 ter 583.2 would accompany the 92 bis statement of Zdravko Krstevski [as interpreted] as I previously said, I would just like to ask to have this document marked for identification, and we will later, when we will be proposing to -- to tender -- to receive in evidence the statement we will attach the criminal reports to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D188, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation], General, good afternoon. Responding to my questions previously, you said that at the time when your committee start with its work that you only had the decision to establish the commission of 13th of August, commission that was established by Mr. Boskoski and the report of that commission while -- while you learned about other documents in a later stage. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the Minister Hari Kostov, did not give you then also the information that he received from Goran Mitevski, an information that the previous minister of defence, Vlado Buckovski, did -- discovered or reviewed after the elections were over in 2002?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have that information available.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the commission did not have the information available, an information that suggested that the president of the Republic of Macedonia was involved in the organisation of this action in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Responding to the previous questions you said that your commission worked in a conditions different than the conditions of the commission established by Minister Boskoski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you worked in the commission, in the public already some names appeared, and you were then able to call those persons and to interview them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, as you said, the commission also on the basis of the interviews of those persons, was not able to come to reliable informations about the person who were in Ljuboten and also was not able to find out what really happened there.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that during the work of your commission that the Albanian population was not willing to cooperate with the Macedonian authorities, especially with the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the situation was much more difficult in 2001.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are able to know this from your position as a person directly engaged in the return of the police forces in the crisis areas. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The ministry, immediately after the signature of the Ohrid Agreement, continued with the previous activity to employ a larger number of Albanians in the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That project started already by the end of 2002 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, it started during the -- by the end of 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It continued in 2001 in cooperation with the American embassy, and the crisis momentarily interrupted the full implementation of that programme. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But right in the beginning of September of 2001, the procedure was continued, an announcement was published in the media, and 107 Albanians were employed at the time in the police, so that was more than the project envisioned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, General, to look at the document in tab 141. That is 65 ter 1D580, page 1D5330, and the English version is 1D5331. General, you see that this is a report which was composed by the department for international cooperation in European -- in European integration of the Ministry of the Interior and it relates to a meeting of the director of public safety with Mr. Gary Bennett, from the US embassy in the Republic of Macedonia. Do you see that this is that document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the report itself says that on the 4th of September, 2001, a meeting was held between the head of public safety, Goran Mitevski and Mr. Gary Bennett, assigned for coordination of the assistance of the embassy of the United States for training of personnel in the area of safety with the aim of reviewing the details of the process of recruiting personnel at the police academy. Does this confirm that the ministry waited no time but right after the conditions were right, continued in cooperation with the American embassy to implement this programme?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that although at the beginning there were -- that it has been envisioned that 100 candidates will be employed out of whom the majority were supposed to be Albanian, that at the end, after this procedure has been completed, 107 Albanians were employed and there was nobody else employed at that time in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even though a large number of Albanians were employed in the beginning of September in the Ministry of Interior, the attitude of the part of the Albanian population to provide the relevant information and to cooperate with the Ministry of Interior did not change, and they continued to be unprepared to cooperate with the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 183. That is Exhibit P104. This is it an Official Note, number 735, and that is an Official Note, as you can see, that was filed by the -- to the department of the internal affairs of Cair and the subject is interview conducted with the person Kenan Salievski. General, do you agree with me if I were to say that it would be important for the police and it would be right for the police to learn about certain information in the village through the heads of that village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From this Official Note, it is visible that Salievski Kenan promised to provide the requested information about the identity of the deceased persons that the Basic Court Skopje I requested, but as it is visible in the last paragraph, and I quote: "On 16th of November, 2001, Salievski Kenan called us by telephone at the department for internal affairs, Cair, and told us that after having consulted the village board from the village of Ljuboten, he cannot give us any information neither about the event nor about the deceased persons." Does this information confirm that also in November 2001 it was impossible for the police to learn about the information that would be important for the execution of a certain procedure in the village of Ljuboten itself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 181, which is 65 ter 1D518. And again it is found on page 1D4744, and the English is 1D4745, and again this is an Official Note of the department for internal affairs in Cair, dated 15th of November 2001, and this is a -- a note about the interview within -- with the persons Selim from the village of Ljuboten. In this note, it is said that an interview was held with a person named Selim from Ljuboten about the event that took place on the 12th of August in the village of Ljuboten, whereby during the fights between the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia and the terrorist gangs stationed in the village of Ljuboten, eight persons have died, and that this Selim has named eight persons that allegedly have been killed and have been buried in the Ljuboten cemetery. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 182. That is 65 ter 1D521, the page is 1D4751, and the English version is 1D4753. We have in front of us now the information that the sector for the interior affairs of Skopje, the department of the interior affairs of Cair, on 19th of November, 2001, have submitted to the Basic Court Skopje II, the department of investigations. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Beneath it says -- it says subject or reference, your file ID number 601/01, of 19th of September, 2001. Do you remember, General, that yesterday we spoke about the fact that, based on the initiative of the Ministry of Interior, initiated to the court and the prosecutor's office, that the prosecutor proposed to carry out investigative actions, exhumation and post-mortem, that at that time a meeting has been held at the institute for forensic medicine, and that it has been clearly concluded that that procedure could only be carried out when additional information would be found about the persons that have been -- that had deceased, about the place where they were buried, and other relevant facts. Do you remember that we were reviewing those documents?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, but it wasn't yesterday; it was on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks a lot. That was really on Friday. The first paragraph of this information, of the department of -- the interior, respond to the request of the court. Tell me, General, is this the way in which the police reacts when they have a file in the hands of the court? The police actually assists the court in response to the requests that are filed to the police by the court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The text goes on saying that an interview has been held with Salievski Kenan, and the content of the Official Note is included, that Official Note that we previously looked at which says that the villagers were not willing to provide the names and other information about the deceased persons. Do you see at this first page that that is now the interpretation of the information that the police -- the police was able to acquire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look the second -- at the second page of the Macedonian version. That is it 1D4752, and the English is 1D4754. The first English paragraph and the second Macedonian paragraph says the following: "In view of the fact that the security situation in this particular region does not permit the undertaking of any kind of operations from our side, we inform you that, apart from the aforementioned, we are not able to perform any other check-ups or investigations and are therefore unable to fully respond to your request. "Regarding the security situation and when it will improve and will become favourable for undertaking of any kind of operations, we inform you that we are able at the moment --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, we are not able to provide an answer to these questions because they do not depend on us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, rather, on higher international and domestic factors. However, should the security situation improves, you will be notified in a timely fashion."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, General, that the head of OVR Cair actually points to the fact that the police of OVR Cair is not able without the assistance of the international community to come to additional information about the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you see at the end that attached to this information the Official Notes 564, 735, and 736 are sent to the court, so the notes that we just looked into. We looked at 735 and 736.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I ask you again: That is the way in which, in accordance to the law the police reacts, when it receives a request from the court, it tries to ascertain the facts that the court is requesting and then about its knowledge or the impossibility to acquire knowledge informs the court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like kindly ask now, I seek for these two documents, 65 ter -- 65 ter number 1D518 and 65 ter 1D521 to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D518 will become Exhibit 1D189. 65 ter 1D521 will become Exhibit 1D190, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, please tell me during the operation of your commission and although maybe you said already something in this regard, is it correct that the representatives of the international community, irrespective whether we are talking about the OSCE or the representatives from the ICTY, they did not submit to you the statements that they received at that time from certain people from the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not submit any notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, they did not submit any other material which would be helpful regarding Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, the position that you used to hold in the police department, probably in the public media you could have acquired knowledge about certain reports from the Human Rights Watch which used to talk about certain alleged atrocities carried out on the civilians in the village of Ljuboten. Were you able to hear such information in the public media?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier or during the time when you were the president of the commission that was established by Minister Kostov, did you receive the Human Rights Watch report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you now to look at the document which can be found in tab 152, and this is 65 ter 1D344. The page is 1D3263. You can find these in the larger second binder, because in the third binder, I think, the documents starts from 155. So the documents in tab 155 onwards can be found in the third binder. So this document can be found in tab 152. Did you manage to find it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document that can be seen on the screen, and you can see on the top left-hand corner it is a Human Rights Watch document, as you can see, and it is addressed to the chief public Prosecutor, Mrs. Carla Del Ponte. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now please turn to the second page of this document. In fact, this would be the third page. This is it 1D3265, and in the second paragraph of this letter, where the report is being send to the Prosecutor of the ICTY, Elizabeth Andersen the executive director of Human Rights Watch writes the following: "[In English] We are troubled by reports that Minister of Interior, Ljube Boskoski in Ljuboten on 12th August that they day that the worst abuse were committed. We respectfully request that your government commence a prompt investigation into his role and the conduct of Macedonian troops under his command." [Interpretation] Now, I ask you to take a look at the document in tab 153. This is Exhibit P352, and I kindly ask for us to immediately look at page which is 000-0101. Beneath you can see page number 3 and in the middle it reads "recommendation." Can you please turn one more page. Yes, very well. This is precisely the page. And, General, I would like to turn your attention to these recommendations. In the first paragraph it reads: "To the Macedonian government." And then it reads: "[In English] Investigates and prosecute the person responsible for the abuses in Ljuboten. Conduct a credible, impartial and transparent investigation into the allegation of government abuses in Ljuboten, including the role of minister of the interior Ljube Boskoski and the forces under his command. The authority who carry out the investigation should be independent from the government agency involved in the Ljuboten operation, particularly the ministry of the interior." [Interpretation] Can you see this recommendation that was provided by Human Rights Watch by which it clearly shows that the forces from the Ministry of Interior cannot participate in the investigation. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the previous note and especially from these recommendations can you see that the Human Rights Watch claims that in the village of Ljuboten the atrocities have been committed by forces under the command of Mr. Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question, General, is the following. After you have collected certain documents and you have interviewed certain people, is it correct that the commission could not clearly define and establish which forces were there in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was not possible to establish who was there in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After you have collected the evidence and you interviewed the people, is it correct that the commission could not establish that those people who were in Ljuboten were under the command of Mr. Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the completion of the work of your commission, on the basis of the evidence that you could collect, you did not at all know whether the people who were in the village were members of the army, the police, or at all they did not -- were not members of the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like for you to look at the document in tab 157. First of all, the document in tab 155, actually. You can find this document in the second binder at the very beginning. And this is Exhibit 1D41. Very well. It is already on the screen. Did you find this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The title is Ljuboten case, ICTY investigation. And the date is 30th of January, 2002. And at the bottom: "[In English] Downgraded to NATO unclassified." [Interpretation] So we are talking about a NATO the document and the transcript was received by the Defence from the Prosecutor's office. In the second paragraph of this document, there is a comment in abbreviation is there which reads Comm. And it reads: "[In English] The Human Rights Watch report on the incident claims that the operation left 10 civilians dead and result in the arrest of more than 100 men." [Interpretation] Can you see this, can you see that this is written here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then it continues: "[In English] And refers to the government newscast of 12 August 2001, to the effect that minister of the interior Mr. Ljube Boskoski was present at the scene that day." [Interpretation] Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From this comment itself, is it clear that future investigation to be led by the ICTY is based on the information that was provided by the Human Rights Watch in its report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I ask you to look at the last paragraph, which reads the following. But before that, in the paragraph, the one before last it reads that Mr. Dzikov - and you know who Mr. Dzikov is - do you know who Mr. Dzikov is? Who was he at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was the chief public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That Mr. Dzikov at that time informed that the investigation team was not able to enter the village on the 12th and 14th of August. And in the last paragraph, you can read: "[In English] The ICTY presented a number of conditions regarding a possible exhumation in Ljuboten. There should be no uniformed police present at the exhumation site and no special forces. Security should be provided by NATO." [Interpretation] Can you see this that at this particular meeting also the representatives of the International Tribunal have laid these conditions, that on the site, on the exhumation, there shouldn't be any uniformed police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the fourth line from the bottom in this last paragraph it says: "[In English] The Macedonian presence at the scene should be remitted to what would be essential for the investigation, the ICTY should be provided with copies of all relevant documents, and if relatives of those buried (the identity of the deceased are apparently known) want to be present at the exhumation site." [Interpretation] So you would agree with me, General, that in the further stages of the implementation of the procedure of exhumation and autopsy, the recommendation of Human Rights Watch has been followed, that is to say, not to allow the police participation in the process of exhumation and autopsy?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will ask you to look at the document in tab 158. This is 65 ter 1D149. Did you manage to find this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that this letter, dated 20th of February, 2002, and as you can see on the bottom of the page, it was sent to Mr. Dzikov, the chief public prosecutor, in the Republic of Macedonia. And on the second page of this document - can you please turn to the second page - one can see that this letter to Mr. Dzikov has been sent by Patrick Lopez-Torres chief of investigations at the OTP office of the ICTY. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will ask to you go back to the first page so that we can see item number 2. So let us see page number 1, items 2 and 4. This is 65 ter 1D149. In the title it says: "[In English] Dear Mr. Dzikov, further to previous meetings with representatives of the OTP and verbal argument in relation to evidence in Ljuboten during 2001, I hereby document and present to you the conditions agreed for the progress of the relevant exhumation and subsequent judicial investigation process." [Interpretation] Item 2 reads: "During the exhumation and investigation process, no uniformed personnel other than the NATO task force Fox troops will be present at the graveyard site." [Interpretation] And then item 4 reads the following: "[In English] No Macedonian special forces, MUP or military will be involved in the exhumation process." [Interpretation] General, this is the 20th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt. I believe that my learned colleague may have misspoke just one word when she began to read the first paragraph after the salutation, dear Mr. Dzikov. That first line reads: "Further to previous meetings with representatives of the OTP, and verbal agreements," my learned colleague said the word arguments and that is what appears in the transcript. Sorry for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for this correction. The mistake is, of course, a result of my poor English and I believe that you approve of that, and it is correct that it reads agreements.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, from this letter is it clearly visible that the Prosecutor from the ICTY communicates with national chief public prosecutor as the only authorised body that in the Republic of Macedonia can propose or instruct the courts how to implement a certain procedure in the criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From these items 2 and 4, is it clear that the ICTY repeats what has been concluded earlier by the NATO on the meeting on the 30th of January, that throughout the process of exhumation and the further investigative process the police cannot be included?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of February, 2002, you were already an under-secretary for police at the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, nobody informed you about these conditions and reasons for which the police cannot participate in the further exhumation and investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Nobody informed me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The common procedure, according to our Law on Criminal Proceeding was that concern tasks and the assistance will be requested by the court from the police and then the police is obliged to provide such an assistance. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The police always has to assist to the Courts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But it is clear that even the procedure that was initiated by the police on the 7th of September, 2001 where it participated by providing certain data and information to the court so the exhumation can be carried out, the autopsy as well, with these conditions, it has been terminated and the further participation of the police was no longer possible in this process. Is there correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, as the most responsible person in the Ministry of the Interior, the under-secretary of police, you were not aware of that, and you were not aware either as the president being the president of the commission established by Mr. Hari Kostov?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, as you previously stated, you could feel that there was a change in the stance of the international community regarding the police, and then by performing your tasks, you could see that there was an obstruction or at least shifting the police away from the further investigation related to the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A few more questions regarding a different topic. Let us go back, first of all, to the reports by the commission -- the first commission.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have read that report, and please tell us whether at any moment you thought that the report of the first commission presided by Goran Mitevski was a false report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never doubted this report, nor I thought that it was a false -- I believe that it was a sincere and precise report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any moment, being the president of the commission, or did your commission came to the conclusion that this report was prepared with bad intent or the purpose was to intentionally hide certain facts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never doubted this report at any moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, General, think at any moment that the commission which was presided by Goran Mitevski conducted a false investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never doubted this at any moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the composition of the commission that prepared this first report, do you agree with me that the Minister Boskoski could rely on the information that they have drafted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That also seems to be asking for a legal conclusion that is in the hands of this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I ask this kind of question previously, and the questions were always related to the issue, because he answered that bearing in mind the composition the minister could rely on their report, and also previously he already relied that bearing in mind the position of the first commission, the minister could also rely on the information that was provided by this commission. I can avoid repeating the questions that were answered on Friday by the witness, but I don't think that there is anything else there to the suggestion -- related to the suggestion and the instructions that you gave me previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will not stop you asking that question, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, having in mind the composition of the commission that was established by the Minister Boskoski, did you, as a president of the commission, and did the commission believe that the Minister Boskoski can rely on their information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Completely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you know that immediately in the Ohrid Framework Agreement of the 13th of August, 2001 they have expressed their readiness for the people who were related to the conflict for them to be guaranteed amnesty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I kindly ask you to look at the document that can you find in tab 185 in the third binder that you have. This is 65 ter 1D163. The page is 1D1724. General, you see here a letter from the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see the coat of arms for the Republic of Macedonia at the top. And then it is signed by Boris Trajkovski, the president of the Republic of Macedonia of that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The letter is sent to George Robertson and it reads the following: "[In English] Dear Secretary-General, I hereby confirm that the NLA will be able to benefit from the opportunities offered by the government for reintegrating into society in accordance with my plan and programme for overcoming the crisis. In this context, the government of the Republic of Macedonia will offer immunity from penal proceedings for all former members of the NLA who have voluntarily disarmed with the exception of those suspected of having committed crimes for which the United Nations International Criminal Tribunal for Former Yugoslavia is competent." [Interpretation] Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a clearly presented will of the Macedonian government and the president to -- to have put under amnesty all those who -- who carried out certain acts as sabotage and terrorist groups at that time in the territory of the Republic of Macedonia except for those who conducted severe criminal acts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that already in November the president, with his decision, pardoned a large number of persons against whom a criminal procedure has been instigated, also pardoned those persons from Ljuboten against whom there has been a procedure before the Basic Court II Skopje in Skopje. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now please look at the document in tab 186. That is Exhibit P83. The page N000-9207, and the Macedonian page is N000-9977. You're familiar with the Law on Amnesty, General, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this law did not make a distinction between the Macedonians and Albanians. The amnesty related to all the persons involved in the conflict. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we look at Article 1, paragraph 2, that is clearly said in the: "[In English] The amnesty also applies to persons who have prepared or committed criminal acts related the conflict in the year 2001, before the first of January 2001." [Interpretation] So not only the persons that committed these acts during 2001 until 26th of September 2001 as it is said in paragraph 1, but also to those persons that have committed such crimes even before the 1st of January, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that was a general Law on Amnesty, and the only excluded those persons against whom a procedure has been initiated in front of the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that has clearly been stated in the last paragraph of Article 1 of this law, which is found on the second page of the law. You could take a look. That is N000-9208 in the English, and the Macedonian -- at the first page, last paragraph in the Macedonian version. So thereby it is said that the provisions of Article 1, 2, and 3 of this Article, do not apply to persons who have committed criminal acts related to and in connection with the conflict in 2001, which are under the jurisdiction and for which the ICTY for prosecution of persons responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law in the territory of former Yugoslavia will instigate proceedings. Is it true, General that when your commission was working that you did not know that the ICTY initiated a procedure against any person in relation to the Ljuboten events, certain defined persons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not informed about the ICTY's activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You only knew that the Prosecution asked to have five cases deferred, among which the Ljuboten case was there, not certain persons, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, we knew about Ljuboten, but we didn't know about the specific persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, General, bearing in mind the legal provisions, would it be true that even if you managed to find some information about some doubts that certain persons have overstepped the authority on 12th of August or the following days, that is in relation with Ljuboten, that in respect with this law you would not be able to carry out any further pre-criminal activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the law -- pursuant to the Law on Amnesty we were not able to initiate any criminal or misdemeanour procedures that were involved in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, if certain procedure has been initiated at the prosecutor's office or in the investigating judge's office, these cases would have had to have been discontinued. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if a certain person would happened to be sentenced, the serving of the sentence would have to be discontinued, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But these are only assumptions, and you already said that the commission were not able to even determine and the reliable facts based on which it would be able to know that some person has committed some criminal act. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As a committee we were not able.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at the time that you used to work, due to the short periods for expiration -- due to the short periods for expiration of the statute of limitation, you were not able to carry out any other activities, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But based on the facts that you determined in the commission, the commission was not able to even determine that some persons have committed some acts that would be disciplinary violations, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this ends my questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I just like to ask Your Honours now to admit in evidence the documents that I showed to the witness. That is 65 ter 1D149, that is the letter addressed to Mr. Dzikov of 20th of February, 2002; then 65 ter 1D344, that is a letter sent by Human Rights Watch to the head of the Prosecutor's office of the ICTY; and 65 ter 1D163, a letter of President Trajkovski sent to the general secretary of the NATO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Each of those will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1D149 will become Exhibit 1D191. 65 ter 1D344 will become Exhibit 1D192. And 65 ter 1D163 will become Exhibit 1D193, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, witness. I wish to inform Your Honours that in cooperation with Mr. Boskoski's Defence all the topics that I wanted to ask about were asked about by my colleague Ms. Residovic and I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski, indeed. Mr. Saxon, would it be worthwhile perhaps having the break at this point, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would be grateful, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would suit the Chamber if we resumed at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies. I would like to mention that the documents that I showed to the witness, I showed document in tab 141.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel repeat the numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D580. That is a meeting between the director of the public security bureau Goran Mitevski and a representative of the American embassy in respect of the employment of the new members in the police that would be of Albanian ethnicity. I apologise, I forgot to tender that document as a Defence exhibit, so I would like to tender it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D194, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Jovanovski, thank you for keeping me honest, General. On Wednesday, this is at page 4897 of the transcript, you explained that in 2001 during joint operations with the Macedonian army, commanders of units of the Macedonian police would receive orders from an army superior, and then the commanders of the police units would issue orders to the police officers in their units who would carry out the operation. Do you recall explaining that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on Friday at page 4977 of the transcript, you explained that if a police officer committed an act of misconduct during a joint operation, the army commander would have the duty to produce an information and inform the police commander. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When the police commander got that information, would the police commander then have a duty to start a disciplinary procedure concerning the police officer who allegedly committed the act of misconduct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, suppose during a joint operation back in 2001, a police commander personally observed one of his police officers, one of his subordinates, committing misconduct, what duty would the police commander have then?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So depending on the region, so in the regions that were not part of the crisis, then it would not be obliged to inform them -- the army commander under whose command he would be, the commander would take disciplinary measures himself, that is to say, would propose disciplinary measures while in the regions that were in the crisis regions, it would inform the army commander and would take an initiative to start a disciplinary measure or for an appropriate punishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So I if I can summarize what you just explained to us. So, then, during a joint operation, a joint army/police operation, if a police commander saw a member of his unit commit an act of misconduct, the police commander would inform the army commander of what had happened, and then the police commander would take the initiative to start a disciplinary measure that was appropriate for his subordinate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned, General -- this was on Friday, and this is at page 4978 of the transcript that during these joint police and army operations there would be morning and evening meetings where issues were discussed between police commanders and army commanders. What kinds of issues would be discussed at these meetings? Can you help us with that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the events. We had both morning and evening meetings. It sometimes happened that we only had a morning or just evening meetings; it depended. We were deciding day by day. At these meetings, the security situation was reviewed and measures and activities were proposed to be taken in the future period, and reports were made about the measures taken in the past period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at these meetings, would the army and the police commanders try to reach agreements as to how to proceed in the future, or the next day or how to resolve particular issues related to the joint operation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And occasionally, were problems of discipline discussed at these morning or evening meetings during these joint operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inter alia, disciplinary events, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And so at that point at a morning meeting or at an evening meeting if a police commander was not previously aware of acts of misconduct or possible acts of misconduct performed by one of his subordinates, the police commander would become informed at one of the meetings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, or in the course of the day, of the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And during or after such joint operations, for example using you as an example, you were a commander of a posebna unit, would the heads of the posebna units inform their superiors in the Ministry of the Interior about their activities whether police officers had been wounded and killed, other important things, other important information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At page 4873 of the transcript, you explained to my colleague that in the first half of 2001 only the Tigers unit reported directly to the minister. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then you explained that all the other police units had their own chain of command within the public security bureau. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who was the person at the top of the chain of command in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the special Tigers unit was under the -- was headed by the minister?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question wasn't directly related to the Tiger unit. Because you had explained that other police units had their own chain of command. They didn't report directly to the minister, like the Tiger units did. They had to work up through a chain of command and so my question is: Who or whom was at the very top of the chain of command in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the uniformed police, the chain goes, commander of a police station is responsible to the head of sector; and then, at the same time, the head of the uniformed police in the sector is responsible to the head for public law and order in the police department. The head of the department for public law and order is responsible to the under-secretary for of police. And the under-secretary is responsible to the director of the public security bureau, while the director is responsible to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who, then, was most accountable for the acts and conduct of police officers in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot talk about the most responsible person because the responsibility is divided each and every one is held responsible for their action.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness, please, a video-clip from 65 ter 988. This is at -- from time code 1:43:27 to a 1:44:05. This is video footage shot on the 15th of May, 2007, after an accident that occurred at a police training exercise at a place called Lajunovo [phoen]. I'm not going to play the entire video clip, I'm just going to play about 30 seconds of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you please ask the Defence counsel to switch on the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware which particular year was mentioned. We received the translation that it was 2007. But, anyways, we would like to know whether this was at the time that is being covered by the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I misspoke. It was video footage shot on the 15th of May, 2002. However it shows -- it contains some speech by the accused Mr. Boskoski which is relevant to his intent and his accountability during the time-period relevant to this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If we can show that video.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Jovanovski, you saw then Minister Boskoski speaking there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he is. This is his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would you agree at least that even Minister Boskoski believed that he was the person most accountable for the activities of the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could understand, he was talking about his actions and not for the rest of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, can we play the video again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you hear the minister say: "As commander of the Macedonian police, he is most accountable." Did you hear him say that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Would you agree with me, then, that even Minister Boskoski believed that he was the person most responsible or accountable for the actions of the Macedonian police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The same as he mentioned at the very beginning of his statement when he said that it is very difficult to determine who is accountable for the events, whether the security or someone else. So this is something that he said as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P437, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Jovanovski, at page 4879 of the transcript, you explained that the police station commander, as a direct superior of the uniformed police, should instigate a disciplinary procedure if one of his officers commits an act of misconduct. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, suppose back in 2001 a police station commander failed to do his or her duty to instigate a disciplinary procedure, who then would discipline the police station commander for failure to do -- for failing to do his duty?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the sector for interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if the head of the sector for the Ministry of Interior fails to do initiate such a proceeding, who would step in then to initiate a disciplinary proceeding?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the sector, he has to assess the situation and give information whether such a procedure should be instigated or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What if the head of sector -- what if the head of the sector fails to carry out his responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we have a professional standards unit or internal control which reviews all the cases and initiates a disciplinary proceeding procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But, of course, that professional standards unit has to be informed about the fact that there was an act of misconduct in the first place. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Jovanovski, can the minister, or in 2001 could the minister inform the professional standards unit about information that an act of misconduct might have occurred?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know -- I didn't understand the interpretation. Can you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Back in 2001, if the minister had information available that a member of the police might have committed an act of misconduct, could the minister provide that information to the professional standards unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the minister had such information, he could have provided it. However, all information is sent in parallel to the internal control to the public security bureau and to the intelligence directorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And would the same concept work with respect to the permanent disciplinary committee? If the minister, in 2001, had information that a member of the police had committed an act of misconduct, could the minister have provided that information or sent a proposal to the permanent disciplinary committee of the ministry to commence a disciplinary proceeding against the police officer, or the member of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Individually, so the minister to initiate a disciplinary proceedings, he wouldn't do that. This would be done by the immediate superiors. So as I already said, the initiative comes from the superiors officers and from the internal control. Now the minister as an official, as an individual, there is a difference here, so if there is certain information during these daily meetings we would review it, and jointly we would submit it to the commission on disciplinary and material accountability.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. And who would have the -- at your daily meetings or at the collegium of the ministry, who would have the final word as to whether such information should be submitted to the permanent commission for disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the director of the bureau or the head of the organisational unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You said probably. If the minister himself felt strongly about an issue of -- related to discipline, could the minister direct that information or a proposal be submitted to the permanent disciplinary commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an information can be sent but a proposal for the initiation of a disciplinary proceedings cannot be done. So just an information, as an information can be given, but for him to give a proposal for disciplinary proceedings, no. So there is a separate commission that would review this kind of information and would decide whether a disciplinary proceeding will be commencing or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sure. But my question is really, did the minister have the authority to instruct his subordinates at the collegium to submit a proposal to the permanent disciplinary commission. That's my question.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He cannot give instructions because the work of the disciplinary commission is provided by the rules. So he can only provide information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could the minister instruct his subordinates to provide such information to the permanent disciplinary commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, this would be done by the immediate superiors or the director.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I know you've said normally. I'm asking whether the minister himself, using his authority, could direct one of his subordinates in the collegium to provide such information to the permanent disciplinary commission.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meetings, it was possible to give not to order if he has received some kind of information, he could convey this information and we would review it and process it. So as a minister, he did not collect any information or process information. This is what is something that is being done by the subordinate services or departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sure. But once the minister had such information, he could direct his subordinates to send that information to the disciplinary commission, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to another topic, General. Last Wednesday - it seems like a long time ago now - at page 4888 of the transcript, you explained to my learned colleague that in 2001, members of the Ministry of Interior tried to take all necessary measures to find -- or to identify the perpetrators of crimes committed against ethnic Albanians in places like Bitola, and parts of Skopje. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall at the time explaining to Ms. Residovic and the Chamber that over 80 per cent of such cases were clarified and finalised and that criminal reports were initiated against perpetrators of Macedonian ethnicity. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, during that process, at that time, how did the members of the Ministry of Interior identify the perpetrators of such acts? How did they do that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was happening in Bitola, and I cannot comment and I can't be very precise about how our colleagues in Bitola did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you a few questions and if you're not able to answer just say so, that's fine. If you don't know, that's fine. Do you know whether your colleagues in Bitola spoke with the victims themselves?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was working in the police department, and these activities are undertaken by the department for forensics or crime police. I don't have plenty of information about the operation of the crime police, at that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, during that period, let's move away from the efforts to clarify the events in Bitola, during the crisis period back in 2001, could the members of the crime police, the criminal inspectors, would they still try to speak with witnesses of a crime? Is that still part of their normal duties?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, we were an open ministry, and we were ready for talking with anybody, anybody that might have come to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Would that include, for example, talking to police officers who might have been witnesses of an alleged crime?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, Exhibit P96. And we'll need to go to page -- we'll be looking at the rule book, I believe, for the organisation of the work of the Ministry of Interior. Yes. Could we move, please, to page 42 of the English version and the bottom of page -- well, and page 25 in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We don't reach seven pages on any of the translations we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If you allow me, Your Honour, to proceed with just using the Macedonian version, I can ask the witness to focus on that so that we understand what it says. Could we enlarge what is Article 167 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see Article 167 at the bottom of the page, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you see where in Article 167 it says that after -- I believe it says after the police possessed sufficient information regarding suspicion that a crime has occurred, they can send a criminal report or should send a criminal report and send it to the public prosecutor. Now we see the English version coming up but we've lost some of the Macedonian version. And I see that in the English version of Article 167 there is a mistake in the translation. It twice says: "Public defender," and that should say "public prosecutor." And, General, if -- do you see where it says, General, that the authorised official composed a criminal report which is delivered to the competent public prosecutor? It's in the first four or five lines.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the actual act of filing criminal charges. So if on the basis of collected information and other undertaken measures and activities in order to confirm or document them, and there is a reasonable suspicion that the criminal offence has been committed which is being prosecuted, ex officio, the appropriate person, official will prepare a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can any authorised official of the Ministry of the Interior who has sufficient information indicating that a crime has been committed compose a criminal report and send it to the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there is a reasonable suspicion, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So that means, then, that the minister of the interior and other members of the collegium, if they have information that provides them with reasonable suspicion, they could compose a criminal report and forward it to the public prosecutor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they have, yes. And this is being done by the crime police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. In other words, the information is being collected by the crime police department.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It collects the material evidence, expert reports and everything else, and like it says here, it is being submitted to the public prosecutor who will then accept or reject such criminal report. So the public prosecutor is the one who has the last word with respect to the submitted criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sure. Okay. I was just a bit confused by your last answer to my last question, because I asked you whether the minister of the interior and other members of the collegium could compose a criminal report and forward it to the public prosecutor. And you answered, if they have, yes. Does that mean if they have sufficient information, yes, they can do that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister and the members of the collegium do not do this. I will repeat it again. The filing of criminal charges is being done by inspectors in the crime police who would collect all the evidence, schematics, photographs, and everything else that can corroborate the criminal charges and this is what is being submitted to the public prosecutor. So the minister is not the person who files the criminal charges nor us as under-secretaries or heads of departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that the filing of criminal reports would not normally be part of the daily work of yourself, your colleagues in the collegium or the minister himself. But you told us a few minutes ago that any authorised official of the Ministry of Interior who has sufficient information indicating that a crime has been committed could compose a criminal report and send it to the public prosecutor. So, just trying to understand, the minister is an authorised official, isn't he? He has that authority, if he chooses to use it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Ministry of Interior, there are several categories of authorised personnel. So we also have cleaning ladies who are authorised but they are not the ones who would file a criminal report. So we know precisely in the ministry who would file criminal reports and who would appear before the court in order to defend such a criminal report, which means that the minister, and we as under-secretaries or heads do not file criminal reports. But as citizens, if we have certain information, we would give this information to the inspectors. This is our civil duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. On Wednesday Ms. Residovic asked you about a working group set up by the Macedonian government for the purpose of collecting evidence about potential war crimes that were perpetrated in Macedonia in 2001. And you explained that in 2001, you were not aware of the activities of this working group. Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you also explained that later on you learned about the existence of this working group concerning war crimes, and you heard that the documents collected by this working group had been destroyed by the new government. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is Exhibit P00081. And this is the criminal code of Macedonia. And if we can turn to page 139 in the English version and page 149 in the Macedonian version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, we're starting here at chapter 34 of the Macedonian criminal code as it stood in 2001. And this chapter is entitled, as you can see, crimes against humanity and international law. Do you see that? I'm not sure if the General can see the title that I just read, because it's -- oh, perhaps he can now. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only see the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And if --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please scroll down on the Macedonian page, please. To see the rest of that page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, we see that Article 403 deals with the crime of genocide. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn the page, please -- and before we do that, the bottom of the English page, we see a subheading: "War crimes against the civil population." Can we turn the page in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see, General, -- we see Article 404 there, war crimes against the civil population, which begins: "A person, who, by violating the rules of international law, during a war, armed conflict or occupation, orders an attack upon civil population, a settlement, certain civil persons or persons incapacitated for combat," et cetera, et cetera, et cetera. And then at the bottom of that paragraph it says: "Shall be punished with imprisonment of at least ten years or with life imprisonment." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then we see at the bottom of the page in English Article 405 is entitled: War crime against the wounded and ill. If we can scroll down in the Macedonian version, please. Maybe if we can turn the page in the Macedonian version. And if we could also, please, turn the page in English version. And I'm very grateful to Ms. Guduric for her patience with me. We see at the top of the next page in English what is described as war crimes against wounded and ill and then we see, war crimes against prisoners of war, use of prohibited combat means, et cetera. Do you see those crimes in the Macedonian version, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, when you and your colleagues refer to war crimes in Macedonia, you're referring to the crimes that are contained here -- were contained here in chapter -- I believe it was 34 of the criminal code? I didn't hear a response, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Then I will repeat it. I will repeat it. The crimes that we've just looked at here in chapter 34 of the criminal code from your country, were these the kind of crimes that were considered as war crimes in Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not that qualified to answer this question of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can remove that exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Last week, General, you answered a number of questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologising to my colleague, I wouldn't like to disrupt, but at page 43/14 of the transcript my colleague said to the witness that the Defence asked him whether he knows whether the Macedonian government established a working group to examine the war crimes. I just would like to point out that my question was at page 4899, line 23 -- 4899, page 4889. And I asked then about the working group established by Minister Boskoski, and there was no mention of any working groups established by the Macedonian government. That's what I would like to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I'm grateful for the clarification. Can we show the witness, please, what is Exhibit 1D182. And if Your Honours still have the binders provided by Ms. Residovic, it would be -- this is the document at tab 87. And that is not the exhibit that I was looking for. That is the Human Rights Watch report. The document I was hoping to see was formerly 65 ter 1D562, which I understood now to have an exhibit number of 1D182. Ah, there we are. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you can, turn to -- do you have tab 87 there in the binder that is with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] You're speaking of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, General, it would be easier for now just to follow along on the screen, please. General, you may recall this document. It was sent by the internal affairs department of Cair on the 26th of April, 2001. And it's an overview of places from which the Albanian terrorists might surface and target buildings of vital importance. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn, please, to the second page in your version, and we'll be looking at, for those following in English, the last two paragraphs in the English version. Actually, the last three paragraphs, I should say, on page 2. General, there's a paragraph, it says: "In the event of the appearance of terrorist groups and a possible threat to the buildings, we recommend the setting up of check-points at the following locations in the area of Cair -- Cair police station." And then there are several locations mentioned. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
