utterances.text: And the next paragraph, it says: "In the area of Mirkovci police station, with the aim of monitoring the situation and preventing any possible threat to the vital buildings, we recommend the following strategic points," and then several points are listed there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, just to be clear, at that time the commander of the sector of the Ministry of the Interior for Cair sent recommendations up his chain of command to the Ministry of Interior in Skopje about the placement of check-points. Is that a correct reading of this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a recommendation but it is an overview. So this is an already completed document whereby the head of SVR Cair provides the overview of places where a check-points would be erected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, you saw the use of the word "we recommend," the words "we recommend," in those two paragraphs, right? You saw that phrase, "we recommend"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not recommends. It would be proposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Would it -- a better English translation perhaps to say we propose the following locations. Is that better?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I'm very -- whether I have expertise in English ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, I'm searching for the right word in your -- I'm searching for the right understanding in your language. And so my question for you is: If you feel the understanding of what is written there is "we propose," just tell us. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document, the proposal is already given. We propose that the check-points are there and there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Okay. What, then, would the members of the Ministry of Interior in the Skopje department do with these proposals?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They accept them and they put them in their operational maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Would these proposals be passed further up the chain of command within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we request, they're sent to us. Otherwise, they remain in their organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And if, when you say "we," you mean persons who were in high-ranking positions within the ministry. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I meant my department and my associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking strictly about this issue, there is a sector for special units that processes these issues. So the under-secretary personally does not deal with these issues. We have a line established whereby -- a communication line who carries out these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I guess my question is simply this. Eventually, who would make the final decision approving or rejecting the proposals coming from -- in this instance, Cair?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The heads of SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Now these check-points, these police check-points that were set up, who manned them, who operated them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mixed active and reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And why was it important to have a mixture of active and reserve police officers manning the check-points?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The total number of active police officers and the tasks -- the tasks given were not able to be carried out in 24 hours only by active police officers. Bearing in mind the terrain that needs to be covered and the time-frame, reserve police officers are called to assist in order to man the check-points and the durations of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. In these mixed groups of active police and reserve police officers at these check-points, who would be in command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the order for execution of duties, a police officer is assigned responsible or responsible worker and it is always an active police officer or an appropriate officer, if there is such a person in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So at these check-points in these mixed groups of active and reserve police officers, the reserve police officers would be subordinate to at least one of the active police officers who was present -- who would be present. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. General, what were the duties or the tasks of the police officers who manned these check-points?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the location of the check-point, they had various duties and competences. For example, if we say that patrol that is patrolling the Djonska [phoen] street that is in the -- inside the city and its task is to control suspicious persons, suspicious vehicles and to carry out preventative actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, for example, suppose we were to reflect upon a check-point in 2001 that was in one of the crisis areas, what responsibilities or duties would the police officers have there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is to control identity, to check the items and persons that are transported, to act preventatively, to receive information, complaints, remarks, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you explained that at the check-point itself, an active police officer would be in charge. Above those active police officers, who would be supervising or commanding the operations of -- of these check-points? Whose responsibility that would be?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police station commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we take a look, please, at what is now Exhibit 1D184. And perhaps we could ask the usher's assistance. It may be that the binder on the floor behind the General might have this tab. It's at tab 131 of the binder provided by Ms. Residovic. The General may need some help because the binder is pretty full and it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, you may recall this document. It was a document that Ms. Residovic showed to you last week. And we see it's a report regarding a meeting between the minister of interior, Ljube Boskoski, the head of the public safety bureau, Goran Mitevski with Ambassador Daniel Speckhard, the assistant Secretary-General of NATO on the 5th of September, 2001. And we see here, again that there is some discussion about how the police check-points were being manned at that time in September of 2001. And you see a little ways down the first page, we see that Minister Boskoski expressed the following with respect to what has been said, because Ambassador Speckhard asked that people at the check-points not be police reservists or members of the special task unit or posebna. And Minister Boskoski replied that: "There are members of the reserve forces of the police at the check-points but not members of the special task unit or posebna." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, how would Minister Boskoski obtain that information about which units of the police were manning the check-points?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most likely, as far as I can see, the director Goran Mitevski was also present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He might have -- he might have had the information from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So this would have been information passed up the chain of command until it eventually reached the minister. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't understand you, what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I guess the information that Goran Mitevski received, would he have received it from lower down on the chain of command? Would that be the normal situation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, was Minister Boskoski the kind of minister who kept his promises to the international community?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Lower down on the page, we see that it says: "Regarding the attitude of the police, Minister Boskoski stated that all members of the Ministry of Interior had been given the rules for conduct of the security forces and that everyone who breaches their authorisations or powers will be held responsible pursuant to the Law on Internal Affairs." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This decision to distribute the rules of conduct to all the members of the Ministry of Interior, who made that decision; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. General, what did Minister Boskoski do pursuant to his affirmation here in the report, in the meeting, what did Minister Boskoski do to ensure that police officers who were deployed at police check-points who allegedly abused their authority or committed acts of misconduct were head responsible, according to the Law on Internal Affairs? What did he do to make sure this happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, as a minister?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is written well here what he stated, that all the members will be issued rules for conduct of the security bodies and everyone that will overstep those authorities will be held responsible pursuant to the Law on the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You're absolutely right; that's what it says here. My question -- and I'm sorry if I didn't make it clear. My question actually goes a step further than what is written here. My question is: After the minister made this commitment that everyone who breached their authority would be held responsible pursuant to the Law. After the minister made that commitment to Ambassador Speckhard from NATO, what then did Minister Boskoski do to make sure that this happened, that persons who violated their authority were held responsible?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a department for police, we took steps, we prepared these brochures that we distributed both to the active and the reserve police officers. And whose idea was it, was it the minister's or the Director Mitevski, I don't know. I don't know whose idea was that. But as we got the order from Mitevski, as a direct superior and we carried it out. We printed them and distributed all these brochures to the people that were manning the check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that. And again, I'm sorry if my question isn't clear. Let's forget for a moment about the distribution of the rules of conduct to the police at the check-point. Let forget about that for a minute, okay? My question actually refers to the rest of the -- the remaining -- the last part of the same sentence, where Minister Boskoski makes a commitment that everyone or anyone who breaches their authority will be held responsible pursuant to the Law. My question is: What measures did Minister Boskoski take, what instructions did he give, if any, to make sure that persons who needed to be held accountable were held accountable?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you say, this commitment refers to all the superior officer who work and who are heading all the subordinates that are manning the check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'm trying to understand your response. Well, what, then, did Minister Boskoski do to ensure that these superior officers did their job in that respect, that they held people who violated their authority responsible? Did Minister Boskoski give instructions to people like you, people in the collegium? What was done to make sure that this commitment was fulfilled?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After these meetings would end, after we have these morning meetings, the positions and recommendations are -- people are informed about these positions taken before the international communities. And we, as subordinates are the ones who would then carry out those recommendations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Based on what you're told to do by the minister?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And did you and your colleagues in the collegium make your best professional efforts to ensure that everyone who breached their authority, police officers manning check-points, were held accountable, according to the Law and Rules of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. On Friday, General, and I'm sorry I do not have the exact transcript page on this point, you agreed with a question put by my learned colleague that in September 2001, with respect to these check-points, the police gave authority to the international community in order to help avoid acts of abuses of power by police officers. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That we provided authority? I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm paraphrasing a question that was put to you by Ms. Residovic on Friday, asking you whether you agreed that, with respect to these check-points and related to this report that we see in front of us, whether certain authority was given to members of the international community, members of NATO or the OSCE to assist in whatever they could at check-points to avoid abuses. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we are not talking about giving authority but a joint cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where we are trying to be open and transparent and to call them to be present at our check-points, the international factors would who would observe and follow police work, so if there is any misconduct for them as an international factor to inform us so that we can undertake the necessary measure for further prosecution. So we are not giving the authority; we just call them for joint cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honours, this discussion occurred on Friday at page 4997 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Just so we understand, General - help us with this - after the Ohrid agreement then, in August of 2001, did the Ministry of Interior's chain of command continue to function?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were orders still sent down the Ministry of Interior's chain of command and reports still sent up the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the Ministry of Interior's disciplinary procedures still function?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They never stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And you personally, General, in your role then as deputy under-secretary, did you continue to give orders to your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were your orders carried out?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very wide question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And did you, General, continue to carry out the orders of your superiors?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, what is now Exhibit 1D185.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this is an announcement that you saw last week, General, from December 2001, where the Ministry of Interior -- of Internal Affairs guarantees that it will not arrest, detain or bring in citizens of Macedonia who are former members of the NLA who voluntarily hand in their weapons. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who gave the order to issue this announcement, this public announcement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall precisely who issued the order for this announcement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Were police officers at the station level, at the OVR level informed about this order, about this announcement and the policy that it contains?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And precisely this announcement created a problem because of the lack of speed of the judicial bodies because they did not disseminate a list of the people who have been pardoned in accordance with the Law on Amnesty. Otherwise, we followed these kind of instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour -- Your Honours, would this be an appropriate time to take the second break? It would be a convenient time for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If that's convenient, Mr. Saxon. We will resume at five past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we please show the witness what is now Exhibit 1D107.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General Jovanovski, it's actually the very first document in the binder that was given to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Your Honours, this was a document that was in the first binder, and I think that we did not bring this first file for the witness, so maybe the witness could be shown this document just on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I could also give the witness my copy, except that...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters would kindly to ask Mr. Saxon, if possible, to turn the right microphone off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please turn to Article 26 of this document, which in the English version is on page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And General Jovanovski, on page 4867 of the transcript on Wednesday, my learned colleague showed you this document. And she reviewed with you Article 26, which provided that the collegium of the Ministry of the Interior is composed of the minister, the deputy minister, the head of the public safety -- public security bureau, the head of the security and counter-intelligence administration, the heads of the departments for police and department for criminal police, and the state secretary. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you were present at a number of the meetings of the collegium in 2001 and 2002. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At page 4869 of the transcript, you indicated at those meetings, that at those meetings, depending on the matters being discussed at the collegium, Minister Boskoski would issue orders to you or to other members of the collegium and then those orders would be passed down the chain of command of the Ministry of the Interior. Do you recall explaining that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn our minds back to Article 26 for a minute. According to Article 26 of Exhibit 1D107, the head of the administration for security and counter-intelligence was also a permanent member of the collegium. And my question then is this: In 2001, depending on the nature of the issue being discussed by the collegium, would Minister Boskoski also issue instructions or tasks to the head of the administration for security and counter-intelligence as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I know that he was present. My question was something different though. My question is: Back in 2001, would Minister Boskoski also issue instructions or tasks to the head of the administration for security and counter-intelligence, depending on the issue that was being discussed by the collegium?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the type of tasks and operations that have been conducted by the administration, during these meetings we did not discuss to a great extent the operations and the work of this administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. But were there times -- were there occasions when the collegium met during the crisis time in 2001, where Minister Boskoski would request that the head of the administration for security and counter-intelligence either carry out a particular task or to try to obtain certain information about what was going on in the crisis areas or some other -- some other issue?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the collegiums, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Apart from the -- apart from the collegiums, can you recall whether the head of the administration for security and counter-intelligence would, depending upon the issue and the problem, try to obtain certain information to assist the minister or the other members of the collegium?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether the head of the administration for security and counter-intelligence in 2001, would, depending on the issue, share information with Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, on Wednesday last week, at page 4877 of the transcript, Ms. Residovic asked you whether Mr. Boskoski ever set up a committee to investigate an issue that had reached him, to shine a light on a certain situation, so to speak, to be informed about perpetrators of certain activities. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you agreed that this was also a manner in which Minister Boskoski tried to learn more information about an issue; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this was specifically for Mr. Boskoski, but every single minister at the ministry would establish such a commissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And on Thursday, starting at page 4941 of the transcript, you explained to Ms. Residovic that as part of your role as a member of the headquarters for Operation Ramno, you received information from the public security sector, as well as from the state security sector, the directorate for security and counter-intelligence. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at pages 4941 to 4950 of the transcript, we can see that Ms. Residovic showed you a number of documents that had been produced by members of the state security sector related to the events in Ljuboten during 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just for the record, Your Honour, I'm referring to exhibits 1D157 through 1D163, and exhibits 1D165 through 1D168. If we can please show the witness what is 65 ter number 251, please. And if we could -- first of all, this is a document, it's dated the 14th of August, 2001. It's from the minister of the interior, office for security and counter-intelligence, sector for analytics research and information, and the title is, Activities of the National Liberation Army in the village of Ljuboten and its surroundings. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this document, the first paragraph, talks about a terrorist group led by Xhavid Asani and Nazmi Sulejman having moved to the area of Skopska Crna Gora where they're preparing to undertake or where they had undertaken preparatory activities to continue their armed activities and terrorist actions against members and buildings of the Ministry of Interior and the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Below that, it says: "The terrorist group has determined the village Ljuboten as their main logistics base." Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then a couple of paragraphs down below, it talks about the mine explosion on the 10th of August at Ljubotenski Bacila where a number of Macedonian army soldiers lost their lives. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, nine soldiers lost their lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we -- can we, in both versions, can we scroll down so we can see the rest of page, please. And then at the bottom it says: "Submitted to Ljube Boskoski, the minister of internal affairs, and Nikola Speceski [phoen], head of the sector for counter-intelligence." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, General, that certain information obtained by the directorate for security and counter-intelligence concerning the events in Ljuboten was also provided to Minister Boskoski? Can we see that from this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P438, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we now show the witness what is Exhibit 1D165, please. And this is a document from the 6th of September, 2001, and it is from the security and counter-intelligence division of the Ministry of the Interior. And it talks about, as we've seen before, a meeting which took place on the 4th and 5th of September, 2001. And the source provides certain information about the events in Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please, in both versions. I'm sorry, can we turn to the very last page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could focus now on that last paragraph. And that last paragraph says: "The aforementioned information that Sali Mamer as a member of a 30-strong paramilitary group was at NLA positions in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August this year, only serves to prove that there were really members of this terrorist group in the village of Ljuboten between 11 and 14 August. And that the action of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia, on 12 August, was undertaken for the neutralization of the terrorists in the area and was not directed against the civilian population of the village, as was recently tendentiously claimed by the humanitarian organisation Human Rights Watch which is striving to present the casualties in the ranks of the NLA as civilian casualties of the supposed repressive Ministry of Interior action." Do you see that? Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, do you think that members -- operative members of the administration for security and counter-intelligence, with their resources and abilities for obtaining information, could have identified the members of the Ministry of Interior who were present in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot understand what you're trying...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, we've seen from these documents and the other documents that my learned colleague showed you last week that the department for security and counter-intelligence, UBK/DBK was able to obtain quite a lot of information about the events in and around Ljuboten, both before the events of August 2001 and even afterwards. So my question is: With all of their abilities for obtaining information, do you think that the members of the administration for security and counter-intelligence could have identified the members of the Ministry of Interior who were present in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a competent person to give this kind of comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. On last Thursday at page 4909 of the transcript, Ms. Residovic asked you whether when the Lions Brigade was established it was composed of existing members of the police, either from the posebna unit or from the reserve police forces, and you replied yes. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall who was the commander of the Lions Brigade in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Goran Stojkov.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What was Mr. Stojkov's job before he became the commander of the Lions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't precisely tell what position he was on. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Do you know if Mr. Stojkov took part in the combat activities during the crisis period in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can take the freedom to say that he never participated in any combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. On Thursday -- actually, let me step back for a minute. How do you know for a fact that Goran Stojkov never participated in any combat activities, if you don't even know what position he held before he became commander of the Lions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because after he became a commander of the Rapid Deployment Unit he was under the command of the police department, of the department for the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the problem was with my earlier question. Before Mr. Stojkov became commander of the Lions, do you know whether he took part in any combat activities during the crisis period in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he never participated in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Then tell us, please, what qualified Mr. Stojkov to become the commander of the Lions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we serve in the army, he served in the special units in the army, and he had such recommendations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify. That he was not the only one who command -- who commanded with the Rapid Deployment Unit, but he had an entire parties below him. He had a platoon commanders and company commanders that were actually commanding with the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What was Mr. Stojkov's relationship like with Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was able to see, it was a professional one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On Thursday of last week, at page 4909 of the transcript, you told the Trial Chamber that no paramilitary groups became part of the Lions, regardless of the fact whether they existed anywhere in Macedonia. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time of the crisis, every -- every of the troops in the regions were called names of animals depending on the area that the animal lives in. We had sarplaninci in Tetovo, we had snakes in -- we had other animals, lynxes, we had an entire zoo. That's what they used to call them themselves, but they didn't act in a paramilitary fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But I guess my question is simply this: During the crisis time in 2001, did paramilitary groups exist?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, what is Exhibit 227, and I'm only going to show the first part of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm asking for Exhibit 227. It is a video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have a photograph with that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I stand -- I stand corrected, Your Honours. This was a clip which my learned colleague showed the witness and it is from 65 ter number 979. It was made in November of 2002 at the ceremony where the Lions received their employment contracts. And it's time code 00:31:16 to 00:32:59.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is a mistake. It is not 2002. I think it is 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I stand corrected. I'm grateful to Ms. Residovic. She's absolutely right; it was November 2001. I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The videos are not in e-court. They must be published by the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Here we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Jovanovski, you heard the commentator saying in the future the Rapid Deployment Unit will be called the Lions as it was called at the time of the fiercest fighting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is just a reporter's comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I know that. And I want to ask you a question about it, okay? At what battle, or battles, did the Lions get their name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking about the Lions, it will take a lot of time. That is connected with the history of the Macedonian nation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I understand that the Lions have a particular symbol, symbolism in the Macedonian nation. The -- and we see the insignia there on -- insignia of the Lion on a person's cap there. But my question is: You heard the comment of the journalist that the Rapid Intervention Unit will be the Lions as it was called at the time of the fiercest fighting. My question is simply this: What operations or combat operations did the Lions or the precursors of the Lions get their name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can freely say that they never received this name in any operation. But the name Lions is connected with the Macedonian history.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can now remove that exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At page 5008 of the transcript on Friday, you explained that -- Your Honour, I would still seek to tender that clip, if I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm hearing from my more organised colleagues today that this clip has already been exhibited. So I will withdraw my request to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we learn the exhibit number so that the transcript reveals it? You're being coached, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is P277.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am very grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So am I.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Moving on to a different topic, General, at page 5008 of the transcript on Friday you explained that according to Macedonian law, the police have no authority to interview persons as witnesses. Do you recall explaining that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall saying this precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Would you take my word for it, or do you want me to ... It was in response to a question from Ms. Residovic where she asked you whether it's true that the Macedonian police have no authority to formally interview persons as witnesses, and you said yes. Does that make sense to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the witnesses are part of a judicial investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But the police do have the authority to collect information from citizens. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: As part of that authority, would a criminal inspector member of the crime police have the authority to speak with police officers who were present at the scene of a crime and gather information from them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they can speak with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is now Exhibit 1D33, please. 1D33. On Friday, General Jovanovski, Ms. Residovic showed you this document at page 5034 of the transcript, and you may recall this is the proposal from the Ministry of the Interior dated the 7th of September, 2001 to the public prosecutor's office and the investigating judge in Skopje that an exhumation be performed in the Ljuboten village. Do you recall that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we now show the witness what is Exhibit P55, please. And I have not done what I should have done, but I'm very grateful to my colleague Ms. Regue for saving me once again. If we can turn to what is N002-1148 within Exhibit P55. Perhaps Ms. Walpita could tell us what -- in terms of the broken down exhibits numbers, what number this would be. I see Ms. Guduric has found it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll see here, General, this is the proposal of the public prosecutor just three days later, to the investigative judge to carry out an exhumation. And so we can see here that the public prosecutor acted quite quickly on the initiative of the Ministry of the Interior. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if this is what it reads here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tell me, General, do you think that the Ministry of the Interior could have proposed that the public prosecutor and the investigative judge identify and interview the members of the Ministry of Interior who were present in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001? Could the Ministry of Interior have made that initiative?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware about it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if the Ministry of the Interior was able to make proposals to take these kinds of initiatives and send them to the public prosecutor and the court, was there anything stopping them from sending other kinds of proposals to the same judicial bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't work in that part of the ministry, so this practice is not familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I understand that the practice may not be familiar to you. But can you think of anything that would have prevented the Ministry of the Interior from making additional proposals to the public prosecutor and the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the -- if the investigating judge would have asked, we as a ministry would have send those information to him. If we had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not asking about sending information. I'm asking about sending proposals, sending initiatives.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the judicial bodies have already started their activities and this is now under the competence of the judicial bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's right. And for that reason, in this case, the Ministry of the Interior took the initiative to send a proposal to the judicial bodies. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would anything have stopped the Ministry of the Interior from providing additional proposals?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. On Friday at page 5012 of the transcript, you explained to my learned colleague that during a meeting of the committee that you led in 2003, you said this: "An Official Note might be prepared. A report or minutes. This is a final document that has three names, so to say, Official Note, report, or minutes. It all depends on the person that would make it and the person who would make it would title it in a certain way." General Jovanovski, can you tell us, please, what do you mean by the term "final document"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A final document, when the meeting is over, or the gathering, so then the final document is being prepared. For instance, when this session finishes then we will have the transcript from today. This would be the final document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Did all such final documents form part of the official record of the work of the 2003 commission that you led?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At page 5017 of the transcript, Ms. Residovic asked you whether, when you led the commission in 2003, you had or could have had documents that were then in the files of the public prosecutor and the courts, and you answered no. Do you remember that exchange?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, can you cite to any Macedonian law that prevents members of the Ministry of the Interior from asking permission to review materials in the files of the public prosecutor or the courts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware whether such law exists. However, the investigative bodies do not provide the files to be reviewed by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But it's not prohibited to ask to see such files, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On Friday, at page 5026 of the transcript, Ms. Residovic asked you whether, from the information provided to the commission that you led by Johan Tarculovski, you could determine whether Johan Tarculovski -- excuse me, whether you could determine whether Mr. Tarculovski was in the village at all and with whom. Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you replied that the commission could not determine this from Johan Tarculovski's statements nor from the statements of other persons who were called to speak to the commission. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at page 5027 of the transcript, Ms. Residovic asked you whether the commission could conclude whether Minister Boskoski had any connection with Mr. Tarculovski with respect to the events in Ljuboten, and you responded no. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I'm wondering if we could give back to General Jovanovski the Prosecution's binder of materials. And if we could turn to what is tab 12 of this binder. It's part of the exhibit marked for identification P00379, and it's also Rule 65 ter 285.12.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn to tab 12, please? You've got it there, General, right? And can you turn to the Macedonian version, please. It's there -- it's there. That's it, General. And if we can turn to page 2 in the English version, in the English version, and page 3 in the Macedonian version, please. And I may need the assistance of the usher to assist General Jovanovski find certain parts in the Macedonian version. If we could have the assistance of the usher, please. This is the Official Note written by Ljube Krstevski on the 19th of November, 2003. There's a typo in the date, in the English version. And if we could turn to page 2 of the English version. And General Jovanovski, if you could take a look at what is the fourth page in the Macedonian version, please. Could you turn to the fourth page in the Macedonian version. And, Mr. Usher, if it would assist, I've highlighted the passage that I'd like General Jovanovski to look at. Can we have the second page of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a slight confusion on the screen. We can see from the Prosecution binder a handwritten text and a translation in English, but as far as we can see, this is not the statement by Ljube Krstevski. So now we don't know whether the Prosecutor wants to show the statement by Ljube Krstevski or the statement by another person, Vanco, or I'm not quite sure what his name is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder, whether, Mr. Saxon, it might be better to continue in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think that would be a prudent course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Might save everybody some time in the long run. You've got something else, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Regardless of the fact that my learned colleague praised me about our organisation of evidence, we still believe that there is some kind of confusion regarding the video footage that my learned colleague wanted to propose or tender as evidence. Namely, as it was mentioned by my colleague, this was a video footage that the Defence counsel presented to the witness, but the Defence presented just P277. However, now, when we checked the transcript with the wording that was said on the video footage that was shown to the witness today, we can see that this is not the same video material. I think that the video footage that my learned colleagues has shown to the witness in the direct examination and it was stopped, and that is why I think that tomorrow it might be good for the learned -- my learned colleagues to see this video again, thus avoiding the possibility for this video to be accepted as evidence, since maybe he would like for this video footage to be tendered into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And we will leave that to the mature reflection of Mr. Saxon overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm honoured, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
